name: Dagaare (Dagaari)
confidence_why: The penultimate-stress rule rests only on Anttila and Bodomo's unpublished 1996 working paper, and the same authors later write that there is little evidence for stress in Dagaare (2009, 2019), analyse the language with a word-initial trochaic foot instead (2019), and leave stress out of both Bodomo's 2021 grammatical sketch and their 2023 tonal analysis, with no independent description to confirm it.
catalog_quote: 2.5 Word stress. Finally, we turn to evidence for stress in Dagaare. Our conclusion will be that stress interacts with both lexical and derived tones, yet it can be identified with neither. ... As for Dagaare, we propose that word stress falls on the penultimate syllable.

Additionally, downstep—a phenomenon in which the second of two high tones is lower than the first (Hyman, 1985; Selkirk & Tateishi, 1991)—is observed and represented as in bʊ́ꜜmá ‘things’. tone_statements.quote: The tone system of Dagaare can be briefly described as follows. There are two tones: H and L. Simple words are typically monosyllabic or disyllabic. Monosyllables surface as either H or L. Disyllables show the expected four surface patterns HH, HL, LH and LL. In addition, there is a fifth pattern H! H with a pitch drop between the two H tones that is conventionally marked by a raised exclamation point. This is contrastive downstep ... Each downstep sets a new ceiling for subsequent H tones making Dagaare a ‘terraced­level’ language
tone_statements.locator: p.444, section 1 Introduction; TBU statement p.448 section 3 + fn.5
tone_statements.summary: Two tones H, L and contrastive downstep !H (not a mid tone); terraced-level; TBU = syllable (Kennedy 1966), no lexical contours; roots may be toneless; floating L triggers downstep; nothing on stress.

tone_statements.quote: In this paper, we examine the lexical tone system of Dagaare (Gur, Niger-Congo), a two- tone language of northwestern Ghana and adjoining areas of Burkina Faso. There is relatively little earlier work on Dagaare phonology. The essentials are described in Kennedy 1966; subsequent work includes Anttila & Bodomo 2000, Bodomo 1997, 2000, Dakubu 1982, and Hall 1977. Kennedy notes that the tone system of Dagaare can be conveniently described by postulating two levels of the register type and a downstepped high unit. In the simple word, which is usually disyllabic, the first syllable can carry either high or low tone, and the second syllable can carry either high, downstepped high, or low tone.
tone_statements.locator: §1 Introduction, p. 2; identity statement p. 3; noun tone patterns §2.1 p. 3
tone_statements.summary: 2 level tones H/L + contrastive downstep !H (three-way contrast after H); TBU = syllable; tonal polarity, downstep, merger as OCP repairs within a tonal foot.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check passes: both the domain quotation sentences are verbatim in the ROA-169 PDF we hold at printed pp.17-18 (§2.5), and the abstract quote at p.1. (2) The classification rests on a 1996 unpublished OT working paper whose stress claim is a theoretical inference from syllable asymmetries and tone attraction, not a descriptive or instrumental finding.
